_comment: The ways one exported wasm FMU can be simulated. Adding one is an entry here and nothing else.
A wasm FMU is what buildModelFMU(..., fmuType="me_cs", platforms={"wasm", <this machine>})
writes: one .wasm component carrying the model kernel, the FMI 3.0 adapter and the model's own
simulation runtime, plus that component compiled ahead of time to a .cwasm. Every runner below
simulates that one FMU through simulate(..., resimulateExecutable="<model>.fmu"), so the
model is translated and compiled once however many of them run.
simflags       what is appended to the model's simulation flags; -s fmi3:… picks the interface.
daeModeSimflags  the same for a model that asks for --daeMode, whose Model Exchange interface is
a DAE one (fmi-ls-dae); a runner without it runs such a model with simflags.
description    what the runner is, for the reports.
branchSuffix   appended to --branch to get the table of this runner; the default is -<name>, so
the FMU's own simulation runtime is the one that needs to say anything here.
The wasm-jit job does not export anything: it translates the model and simulates it the way
simulate() does, filling the wasm-jit table. The sim runner below drives the exported FMU the
same way, and is what the older job that tested all three from one export used; naming it
alongside me and cs would write the FMU's results into the wasm-jit table.

sim.description: the FMU's own simulation: the translated model run by omc's simulation runtime, as simulate() runs it

me.description: FMI 3.0 Model Exchange, integrated by omc with the model's own solver (DASKR unless its annotation says otherwise; IDA over the fmi-ls-dae residuals for a --daeMode model)

cs.description: FMI 3.0 Co-Simulation, the FMU integrating itself with DASKR
